topics.title: When does Nature become a resource?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain when an element of Nature comes to be seen as a natural resource.
Apply the conditions of technological access, economic feasibility and cultural acceptability to decide whether something is a resource.

topics.title: Categories of natural resources by their use

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the resources without which life could not exist on Earth.
Recognise natural resources that humans turn into useful and beautiful objects.
Identify natural sources of energy and see that one resource can serve several uses.
Distinguish between restoration and regeneration as principles of Nature.
Explain why renewable resources stay renewable only if Nature's rhythm is not disturbed.
Distinguish ecosystem functions from the ecosystem services humans receive.
Define non-renewable resources and identify examples such as fossil fuels and metals.
Suggest judicious uses of non-renewable resources and renewable substitutes.

topics.title: Distribution of natural resources and its implications

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the uneven distribution of resources shapes settlements, trade and industry.
Weigh the benefits of resource-based industries against costs such as displacement.
Explain why resources that cross political boundaries lead to sharing disputes.
Explain the meaning of the natural resource curse or paradox of plenty.
Evaluate how investment in industry, skills and governance can overcome the resource curse.

topics.title: Stewardship: restoring and regenerating renewable resources

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the causes and effects of groundwater over-exploitation, as in Punjab.
Explain how traditional and organic practices restore soil health, as in Sikkim and Vrikshayurveda.
Describe the pollution caused by cement and the move towards alternative materials.

topics.title: Responsible and judicious use of resources

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the need to shift to renewable energy, with the International Solar Alliance as an example.
Evaluate fair access to resources and the idea of lokasangraha in acting as stewards of Nature.
